title: Avesta — Sîrôzahs, Yashts and Nyâyis
dateDisplay: c. 1st millennium BCE, with later additions
attributionNote: The Yashts are anonymous hymns addressed to individual divine beings. They were composed over several centuries and collected in the Avestan corpus; none is ascribed to a named author.
description: The Sîrôzahs, Yashts and Nyâyis are the devotional hymns of the Avesta: invocations of the thirty days of the month, twenty-four longer hymns addressed to Mithra, Anâhita, Tishtrya, the Fravashis, Verethraghna and the other Yazatas, and the short Nyâyis prayers to the sun, moon, water and fire. They preserve Zoroastrian myth and cultic poetry outside the liturgy of the Yasna.
historicalContext: The Yashts are the principal surviving source for Zoroastrian mythology and for the cult of the Yazatas. James Darmesteter translated them for the Sacred Books of the East, volume 23 (1883), with the Sîrôzahs and Nyâyis, and his notes identify the Vedic and later Iranian parallels.
availabilityNote: Complete for this volume. The Sîrôzahs, all twenty-four Yashts and the five Nyâyis are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one hymn per chapter. The volume's introduction and preliminary observations are not part of the work.
